column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE: Square Enix / Lancarse, Unreal Engine 4 (the HD-2D engine: 2D sprites on a 3D scene), SDK 20.5.17, NVN, CRIWARE sound and movies; update 1.0.1 (v65536).
# The card is a Switch 1 cartridge (the game also ships for Switch 2): its secure partition holds the base game, the update and one DLC (a licence only).
# the on-screen gamepad of the iPhone app: the full layout (D-pad, right stick, L3 / R3) as the other Switch titles
# the card is the Korean release: the game has ko, zh-Hant and zh-Hans
# subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie (main imports from it)
# Unreal Engine: nninitStartup reserves one address region for the whole engine (62 GB by default, the engine's own value) and the engine's FMallocBinned3 takes 38 GB of it
# (main+0xae82c: the size 0x980000000 is hardcoded in the game and does not follow -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=, so that switch cannot help).
# The engine's own address region is capped to 40 GB (-SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= in MB: the 38 GB pool has to fit in it, the SDK's
# 1 GB node area is taken from the alias region before it, and regions of 1 GB and more are 1 GB aligned), and the alias region is 44 GB (the 62 GB region, 1 GB aligned) with a 48 GB reservation.
# The sizes are cut down from 64/68 GB so that the one mmap the host makes for the whole guest address space fits in an iPhone's address space: with the
# com.apple.developer.kernel.extended-virtual-addressing entitlement (the kernel's jumbo mode) an app gets 64 GB of address space, without it about 2-7 GB (the
# engine's 38 GB does not fit and the host dies with "reserve guest AS").
# the NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource
# the shaders' texture handles: some of them are dynamic (the translator cannot trace them to one slot), the
# game picks them from the c2 tables at run time
# The shaders are UE5's shader cache records in the .ucas of the IoStore (FFRS/Content/Paks/FFRS-Switch.ucas), not in a .ushaderbytecode archive: each record holds
# one stage's code area and control section (uepak.py io, the same LSLG records as Octopath Traveler 0's archives)
